data.name: Bhagavathi
data.gender_notes: Bhagavathi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Bhagavathi is the name of a Hindu goddess, often depicted with multiple arms holding various symbols of abundance and prosperity. She is revered as the goddess of wealth, fertility, and prosperity. The name Bhagavathi is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘bhag’, meaning fortune or wealth. The name Bhagavathi carries the meaning “Goddess of Wealth and Prosperity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bhagavathi usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of wealth and prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of divine blessings and prosperity
data.etymology: Bhagavathi belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Wealth and Prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bhagavathi total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: Bhagavathi is a symbol of power, prosperity, and abundance in Hindu culture. In many Hindu communities, especially in the southern parts of India, devotion to Bhagavathi is seen as a means to attain material and spiritual wealth. Bhagavathi temples, filled with vibrant colors, are bustling with devotees during festivals and on special occasions.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Bhagavathi signifies the divine blessings of Fortune, prosperity, and the ability to overcome adversity. For Hindus, the goddess represents the divine feminine, a source of power, strength, and nourishment. She is a reminder of the universal truth that material and spiritual wealth are interconnected and that both are essential for a fulfilling life. Invoking the blessings of Bhagavathi is believed to bring peace, happiness, prosperity, and good fortune.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bhagavathi is the divine feminine embodiment of divine blessings and nurturing love. Her name signifies the bestower of bhagas or divine grace, fortune and prosperity. She is revered as the Goddess of wealth, fertility, and happiness.

historical_references.reference: Bhagavathi is mentioned in the ancient Indian epic Mahabharata. She is referred to as the goddess of prosperity, fertility and wealth. She is also considered as the mother goddess and the protector of villages and crops.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India, the other being the Ramayana. It is attributed to Vyasa and is traditionally believed to have been composed between the 4th and the 2nd centuries BCE. The epic narrates the story of the Kurukshetra war between the Pandava and the Kaurava princes.

historical_references.reference: Bhagavathi is also identified with the goddess Durga. The goddess Durga is mentioned in the Devi Mahatmya, an ancient Indian text that is part of the Markandeya Purana. Bhagavathi is considered as one of the ten forms of Durga, and is worshipped as a protector against evil and as a bringer of prosperity and wealth.
historical_references.context: The Markandeya Purana is one of the eighteen major Puranas of Hinduism. It is believed to have been composed between the 6th and the 8th centuries CE. The Devi Mahatmya is a part of this Purana, and it glorifies the goddess Durga and describes her various forms and her defeat of various demons.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Bhagavathi' is often associated with the Hindu goddess of power, fertility, and wealth. In modern contexts, this name is celebrated and revered across various platforms. On social media, numerous accounts and groups are dedicated to the worship of Goddess Bhagavathi, sharing prayers, rituals, and devotional art. In art and culture events, Bhagavathi is depicted as a powerful and nurturing figure, inspiring creativity and expression. In religious and spiritual practices, the name 'Bhagavathi' is invoked during rituals and puja, symbolizing the divine feminine and the abundance of nature.
